anchor: In March 2026, Marlow District Council closed the Kingfisher footbridge

anchor: corrosion in two of its four main cables

sources.quote: Corrosion has reduced the effective cross-section of cables C2 and C3

note: Two cables (C2 and C3) had significant corrosion; however, cables C1 and C4 also show surface corrosion. The claim focuses only on the two worst-affected cables.

anchor: about 3,000 pedestrians a day
claim: About 3,000 crossings a day.

sources.quote: Council pedestrian counts for 2025 give an average of 2,900 crossings per day, rising to 4,100 on market days
an average of 2,900 crossings per day, rising to 4,100 on market days

note: About 3,000 (doc rounds 2,900) is the average. The source specifies this is an average not a peak; peak is 4,100 on market days. Suggest: 'average of about 2,900 pedestrians a day'. The source figure is an average of 2,900 crossings per day (4,100 on market days), and counts crossings rather than pedestrians. 'About 3,000' is a fair rounding but the document should say average crossings. Suggest: 'an average of about 2,900 crossings a day'.
hint: Check the count and whether it is an average or a peak.

anchor: water had been pooling at the west anchorage since at least 2019, when a previous inspection first noted the problem

anchor: closed the bridge on 14 March, two days after the report was published

closed to the public on 14 March 2026
closed to the public on 14 March 2026 following receipt of the Halden Associates inspection report dated 10 March 2026

note: The closure was 14 March; the report date was 10 March (4 days), not 12 March (2 days). The arithmetic holds only if using the document's claimed publication date of 12 March, but the actual report date is 10 March. Suggest: 'four days after the report was dated'. Closure on 14 March is supported, but the report is dated 10 March, so the gap is four days, not two. The 'two days' arithmetic depends on the wrong 12 March date. Suggest: 'closed the bridge on 14 March, four days after the date of the report'.

anchor: a temporary fix would be throwing good money after bad
claim: Verbatim quote of the council leader.

sources.quote: The Leader of the Council said that a temporary fix would be throwing good money after bad unless the drainage was also corrected

note: The quote is accurate but incomplete. The source includes a critical condition: 'unless the drainage was also corrected'. Suggest: 'a temporary fix would be throwing good money after bad unless the drainage was also corrected'. The quote is trimmed at a condition: the leader said a temporary fix would be throwing good money after bad 'unless the drainage was also corrected'. Cutting the condition turns a conditional into a blanket rejection of temporary repair. The minutes also record this as reported speech, not a verbatim quotation. Suggest: 'The minutes record the leader of the council saying that a temporary fix would be throwing good money after bad unless the drainage was also corrected.'.
hint: Is the quote complete? Does the source attach a condition?

anchor: foot traffic has moved from the east bank to the west bank
claim: Since the closure people stay on the west bank rather than the east.

sources.quote: commuters and shoppers arriving at the station on the east bank no longer cross to the west bank
Several traders said customers were staying on the east bank

note: The document claims traffic moved FROM east TO west bank, but the source shows the opposite: people arriving at the east bank (station) are NOT crossing to the west bank (market square), meaning they stay on the east bank. The direction stated in the document is backwards. Direction reversed. The Gazette says people arriving at the station stay on the east bank and no longer cross to the west; the document says traffic has moved from the east bank to the west bank. Suggest: 'foot traffic that used to cross to the west bank now stays on the east bank'.
hint: Check the direction against the Gazette.

anchor: the council has promised a shuttle bus by 1 May

a shuttle bus between the station and the market square was expected to be running by 1 June
